title: Chaupai close
hook: a short prayer for the times you feel unsafe
tomorrow: Anand Sahib: the song of bliss

segments.voice: Yesterday, duaar, the last couplet, and your line, your door. Today, the whole Chaupai, and where it lives.

It's late. The lights are off, the house has gone quiet, and that's exactly when the mind gets loud. The thing someone said at work. The test results that aren't back. The noise outside that's probably nothing. Night makes every worry bigger. Some people turn on a podcast. Some scroll. Many Sikhs say a short prayer they know by heart, and for some, the one they reach for in the dark is the one you've spent ten days with.
screen: `LATE, LIGHTS OFF, MIND LOUD.` → `NIGHT MAKES WORRY BIGGER.` → `A PRAYER KNOWN BY HEART.`

segments.voice: Lay the prayer out end to end. A humble request, benti, in four-part verse. Protect me, giving me your hand. May my heart's wish be fulfilled, and my mind rest at your feet. End the enemies, outside, and for many Sikhs, inside: the five thieves. Carry my servants and Sikhs across the river. Then the prayer looks up: the Creator spreads creation out and gathers it in, knows every heart, and recognizes the pain of the good and the bad. Then, charan: since I held your feet, I look to no one else. And at last, leaving every other duaar, I have come to yours; Gobind is your servant. Ten days, one prayer, one movement: keep me. Where does it live in a Sikh day? In the morning, as one of the five banis of the Nitnem. In the evening, inside Rehras, the prayer said at dusk. At the amrit ceremony, recited as the water is stirred. And for some Sikhs, in the unscheduled moments too: before a long drive, at a hospital bedside, on a plane, in the dark. Ahead on this path you'll meet Kirtan Sohila, the bani many Sikhs say last thing at night. Chaupai isn't a replacement for that. It's more like the pocket prayer, the one that fits in the gaps: short, personal, asking for something very basic. And it was written by someone who knew real danger, so it never pretends danger isn't real. It just asks, in the middle of it, to be kept.
screen: `HAND, HEART, ENEMIES, THE RIVER.` · `SPREADS, GATHERS, KNOWS THE PAIN.` · `THE FEET, THEN THE DOOR.` · `MORNING, DUSK, AND THE GAPS.` · then, large: `KEEP ME.`

segments.voice: Choose the line from Chaupai you'd want in the dark: the hand, the heart's wish, he knows the pain, or every other door. Say it slowly a few times, in the original if you can, in English if you can't, breathing between, until it starts to feel familiar. If you pray, you can join it to Waheguru.

Chaupai Sahib, the Tenth Guru's prayer for protection. Ten days with it: the hand, the heart's wish, the enemies, the river, the knower of hearts, the feet and the door, folded into two words: keep me.
Your line: keep me. Two words, small enough to carry into the dark. Ten days of Chaupai, done.

screen: `DAY 379 COUNTS.` → `CHAUPAI, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: ANAND SAHIB: THE SONG OF BLISS.`

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite Chaupai Sahib in the morning Nitnem and within the evening Rehras, and many also say it at night, before travel or in times of fear; Kirtan Sohila is the bani usually said before sleep.

original.note: Gurmukhi: Chaupai Sahib, the honored name for the Tenth Guru's prayer for protection.

trapdoor: what you thought: a prayer for when things go wrong.
what it means: one movement in ten days of lines, from a hand to the feet to a door: keep me, in the morning, at dusk and in the dark.
what a scholar hears: Chaupai is one of the five Nitnem banis, is embedded in Rehras, and is read at amrit preparation, three liturgical homes for one short poem.

chat.says: You said you sometimes say Chaupai Sahib at night. What's it actually asking for?
options: To be kept: a hand to hold, the heart at the Guru's feet, shelter at his door.
Mostly for wealth and success, so that tomorrow goes well at work and home.
Nothing, really; it's a thank-you for the day that doesn't ask for anything.
chat.meaning: Chaupai is a benti, a humble request: from protect me, giving me your hand, to leaving every other door for yours. In two words: keep me.
